analyst.summary: Berger Paints' FY26 shows a volume recovery (Q3 +8.5%, Q4 +11.8% YoY, the latter a 12-quarter high) running well ahead of value growth (Q1 +3.6%, Q3 +0.30%, Q4 +6.07%), the fingerprint of an industry-wide price war against Birla Opus (Aditya Birla Group's 2024 entrant, now ~6.6-10%+ decorative share and scaling to 1,332 MLPA capacity) layered on Asian Paints' still-dominant >50% share; full FY26 consolidated PAT fell 4.6% YoY to Rs 1,128 cr despite a strong Q4 (PAT +27.5% YoY, EBITDA margin at a 10-quarter high of 16.79%), the decline explained by a Q1 FY26 Rs 36.81 cr exceptional fire loss (since reversed on insurance) plus a weak, competitively-pressured Q1-Q3 base. At Rs 491/share (20-Jul-2026), 49.1x trailing P/E and 8.28x P/B against 17.8% ROE, the stock prices in more pricing power and growth durability than the last four quarters of muted value growth have actually delivered, even though the FY26 margin recovery itself came mostly from softer crude-linked input costs rather than repricing. Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter) results are PENDING, board-meeting date not yet fixed, legally due by ~14-Aug-2026 -- the next real read on whether Q4's volume reacceleration is durable or a soft-base blip.
